profile.name: Shamia e Beqarit
profile.tagline: An Albanian wedding ritual dance concluding with the burning of a bachelor's handkerchief.
profile.insight: Performed as the final act of an Albanian wedding, the bride and groom dance while ritually burning a bachelor's handkerchief.
profile.profile: Shamia e Beqarit is an Albanian traditional dance and ritual always practiced during wedding celebrations. It serves as the final dance of the event, performed by the bride and the groom. A defining moment of the ritual involves the burning of the handkerchief of the bachelor. Wedding participants accompany the entire performance with singing.
profile.profile_long: Shamia e Beqarit is documented as an Albanian traditional dance and ritual. It is always practiced in the Albanian wedding context as the final dance of the celebration. The performance is executed by the bride and the groom. A central feature of this ritual is the burning of the handkerchief, known as the shamia, of the bachelor, known as the beqarit. The entire performance and dance are accompanied by a song sung directly by the participants of the wedding. Detailed techniques, musical meters, and historical origins remain undocumented in the primary sources.
